subject: Post-demo: long-context model fit + evaluation plan for Praxis Health
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Carver <alex.carver@praxishealth.com>, eval@praxishealth.com
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: long-context model fit + evaluation plan for Praxis Health

Alex — great to meet the team today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum: 

What we heard
- Primary goal: extract structured clinical events and patient-level summaries from multi-page visit notes (20–60 pages, mix of SOAP + templated sections).
- Constraints: need high fidelity for medication changes and problem-list items; summaries must not lose timeline fidelity.
- Non-negotiable: data residency for PHI (you asked about our Private deployment options).

Redwood's immediate recommendations (model + eval focus)
- Long-window candidate: redwood-long-13b-64k (fast, lower cost than the 65B, good for summarization fidelity on clinical templates)
- High-quality baseline: redwood-65b-xlong-64k (stronger instruction-following, best for long-chain temporal extraction)
- Fallback (latency-sensitive paths): redwood-llama2-70b-8k quantized (use for short extracts only)

Why these? In our internal benchmarks the 13b-64k profile kept medication and timeline facts >92% on our templated clinical tests while cutting token cost ~40% vs the 65B. The 65B remains the most robust for noisy notes with lots of OCR-like artifacts.

Artifacts I attached
- praxis_longcontext_benchmarks_v1.csv (token-level precision/recall across 30 canonical clinical cases)
- praxis_prompt_set_v2.txt (collection of prompts and control prompts we used for the CSV)
- cost_projection_64k.pdf (high-level unit economics for 64k-window runs at your expected throughput)

Immediate ask / next steps
1) Can you share 8–10 redacted (PHI-free) representative notes we can run through the prompt_set_v2? Prefer a mix: 3 templated, 3 long consults, 2 noisy/OCR. (Alex: you mentioned redaction this week — great.)
2) If you want, we can run a 10-case pilot on hosted Redwood with a short NDA (we can scope via the HubSpot deal). Expected turnaround: 3 business days for initial results.
3) Schedule: propose Tue 6/22 10:00am PT for a 30m debrief of the pilot output. Let me know if that works.

Flagging potential quality regression risks up front:
- Truncation during large prefixed context (we saw some title-header duplication causing artifacts at ~48k tokens)
- Template-heavy sections can induce hallucinated timeline merges if prompts don't explicitly anchor by section headers

I'll ask Neha and Marissa to coordinate pilot logistics and run the initial sanity checks on your sample. Thanks again — excited to dig into this.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(sean.gallagher@redwood.com)

Attachments: praxis_longcontext_benchmarks_v1.csv (CSV), praxis_prompt_set_v2.txt (TXT), cost_projection_64k.pdf (PDF)
From: Alex Carver <alex.carver@praxishealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: eval@praxishealth.com, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 18:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: long-context model fit + evaluation plan for Praxis Health

Thanks Sean — appreciate the clear plan and the artifacts. Couple quick clarifications: 

1) Redaction: we can provide 10 notes redacted by Monday EOD. They will be exported as PDF (OCR noise present in some). Is that format okay?
2) For the pilot, we need to confirm whether the hosted run will touch PHI. Our security folks may require Private deployment for any PHI. Can you confirm: can the initial 10-case run be on a pseudo-PHI set (deidentified) in hosted mode for speed, and then move to Private for full PHI?

Also — on models: is the redwood-long-13b-64k expected to keep section anchors (e.g., "Assessment/Plan") intact in the extract? We've had previous runs where headings got collapsed into the running summary.

Alex
Alex Carver
Lead Data Scientist, Praxis Health
(alex.carver@praxishealth.com)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Carver <alex.carver@praxishealth.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: long-context model fit + evaluation plan for Praxis Health

Alex — quick answers and operational notes from our side.

1) Format: PDF with OCR noise is fine; please include the raw PDF and a text-extracted version if available (we use both).
2) PHI / hosting: yes — initial 10-case pilot can be done on deidentified data in Hosted for fast turnaround (we'll treat it as non-PHI). For any PHI-run we will provision a Private deployment; team will send a SOC2 + architecture brief.
3) Section anchors: good catch — the 13b config preserves explicit headings when prompts include an anchoring instruction (we call them "section-aware prompts"). See the attached praxis_prompt_set_v2.txt — prompts 4–6 are designed to keep Assessment/Plan and Medication lists as discrete outputs (we include an example output schema).

Operational next steps (who does what)
- Praxis: upload 10 redacted/deidentified PDFs + optional plain-text extracts to the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/praxis-eval-2027
- Redwood (Marissa): will run the 10-case pilot on redwood-long-13b-64k and redwood-65b-xlong-64k, produce a short CSV with per-case precision/recall and a short notes document with failure-mode examples (expected deliverable by Wed EOD)
- Redwood (Neha): follow-up with security package (SOC2 + Private deployment brief) and HubSpot update for the deal (D-98321)

I also added two tests we consider critical: medication-change precision and timeline ordering (we included these in the CSV). If you want, we can add a specific prompt variant that forces extraction by header (will cost an extra pass).

Proposed meeting: Tue 6/22 10:00am PT stands for the debrief. Invites to follow.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(neha.kapoor@redwood.com)

Attachments referenced: praxis_prompt_set_v2.txt
From: Alex Carver <alex.carver@praxishealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: long-context model fit + evaluation plan for Praxis Health

Thanks — we'll upload the set (PDFs + text extracts) to the Drive link today. Two quick asks before the pilot runs: 

- Can you include a short example of the "section-aware" prompt and expected JSON schema in the pilot deliverable? Helps our engineering team map fields directly into the ingestion pipeline.
- For the cost projection, can you show per-case token estimates for both 13b-64k and 65b-64k (so we can model costs at 5000 notes/mo)?

If those two are included in the Wed deliverable, we should be able to sign off internally and move to a Private pilot right after. Looking forward to the debrief.

Alex
